I've been working this land since I was ten years old. I know the soil here in Quzhou — it's sandy loam, low in organic matter, needs water every few weeks in summer or the cotton suffers. My father grew cotton here too. This is what I know.

My 20 mu is split how I always do it: 12 mu for cotton, which is my main income, and the other 8 mu I rotate wheat in winter and maize in summer. Some of my sons work in the city now, so I can't always count on extra hands during peak seasons. I keep the work manageable.

**Cotton (12 mu):** I buy Bt hybrid seed from the county seed station every year — it handles the bollworm better than the old varieties. I plow deep in spring before planting. I put down phosphorus and potassium as base fertilizer, then top-dress with urea when the plants flower. I water by well five times: before planting, at bud stage, flowering, boll formation, and boll opening. I still spray four or five times for aphids and red spider mites — Bt doesn't stop those. I expect around 300 jin of seed cotton per mu, same as last year.

**Wheat (8 mu):** I sow Jimai wheat in October after plowing. Four irrigations — before winter, at jointing, at heading, at grain filling. I spray twice, once for rust and once at heading for disease. Yield should be around 480 jin per mu.

**Maize (8 mu):** After wheat harvest in June I rotary till and plant Zhengdan 958 straight away. Three irrigations. Two pesticide sprays for corn borer and ear rot. I expect 600 jin per mu if the rain is decent.
